transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-02
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Jordan Park (Corvus Head of ML), Samir Patel (Product), Lee Chen (InfoSec), Marta Ruiz (Data Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Redwood and Corvus scoped a 4-week POC focused on a quality evaluation plan and regression playlist. Main goals: define success criteria (accuracy / hallucination targets / format adherence), size workload for perf and quality benchmarks, agree on golden prompts and regression sets, and set timeline for baseline runs + tuning. Security and data residency questions flagged by InfoSec. Next steps and owners captured.

Topics covered:
- Success criteria and acceptance gates
- Golden prompts and regression dataset sizing
- Hallucination detection approach and format checks
- Scoring approach (auto metrics + human eval)
- Performance benchmarks and expected load
- POC timeline and decision checkpoints

--- Transcript (timestamps approx every ~30-45s):
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick intro — Alex from Redwood, i run the accounts for southeast enterprise. with me is Priya, our solutions engineer.
[00:09] Priya: hey all — hi, Jordan, Samir, Lee, Marta — excited to dig in on the eval plan.
[00:14] Jordan: thanks Alex. short background — we are replacing a few heuristics in our question-answering pipeline with a LLM backend. primary goals are accuracy and removing hallucinations in finance-related responses. latency nice to have but not first order.
[00:28] Samir: product is most worried about consistent formatting for our downstream parsers — we can't have free-form answers that break the ingestion.
[00:34] Lee: and InfoSec — we need to know what stays on-prem vs what leaves, KMS, and audit logs, SOC2 stuff.
[00:40] Marta: from data eng we'll supply a sample slice and can annotate entity ground truth for a subset.
[00:45] Alex: perfect. high level, we usually run a 3-4 week POC: Week 0 onboarding + golden prompt curation, Week 1 baseline runs and perf, Week 2 iterative tuning (quantization / batching / prompt engineering), Week 3 final eval and handoff. we can be flexible. does that match your expectations?
[01:02] Jordan: yes that maps well. with two caveats — we need a clear definition of pass/fail for quality (cannot be fuzzy) and we need to size the workload to reflect our bursty traffic.
[01:13] Priya: totally, that's what today's call is for. i'd like to propose a concrete success criteria bundle so everyone can sign off.
[01:20] Samir: go ahead.
[01:22] Priya: okay, proposed acceptance gates: 1) accuracy or correctness on golden prompts: minimum 92% exact-match or intent-correct for the curated golden set; 2) hallucination rate under 1.5% as measured by entity-level hallucination detector on regression set; 3) format adherence >= 99% for the structured-response tasks; 4) p50 latency under 250ms in dedicated mode for 1rps baseline, and 99th percentile under 1s for peak loads — these perf numbers can be optional if you choose hosted vs dedicated.
[01:58] Jordan: can you clarify the hallucination measurement? how do you detect hallucinated facts vs paraphrases?
[02:06] Priya: good question. we do a two-stage approach: automatic detectors that match entities and facts against your ground truth (entity-level checks), plus spot human-annotated review for high-risk cases. automatic stage flags candidate hallucinations when generated spans contain entities not in the source or contradict known facts; then a small human panel reviews a stratified sample to estimate the true hallucination rate.
[02:37] Lee: and for security, anything flagged as PII or exfiltration needs audit logging — can Redwood provide request/response logging with redaction options?
[02:46] Alex: yes, we have configurable logging — token-level traces are optional, and we support VPC/private deployments with customer-managed KMS for on-prem keys. we'll include the SOC2 appendix in the pack.
[02:57] Marta: for golden prompts how many do you usually need? we can definitely produce examples but need a target.
[03:04] Priya: for this use case i'd recommend 300-500 gold prompts covering both happy-path and edge-case intents. golden prompts should be labeled with expected output (exact format) and severity (must-not-hallucinate vs guidance). regression set should be larger: 2k-5k cases, including adversarial examples and historical failure cases.
[03:28] Jordan: 300 sounds doable. for regression, can we include historical user logs? those are messy.
[03:33] Marta: we can provide de-identified logs but we'll need to run them through a filter.
[03:37] Priya: good — we'll provide a small script to sample and canonicalize logs into test cases (we'll drop sensitive fields unless you want to use VPC/private evaluation).
[03:47] Samir: about scoring — is this a pure automated score or will you include human grading?
[03:51] Priya: it's a hybrid. autometrics first: exact-match, token-level F1, normalized string matching, entity precision/recall. then human-eval for a statistically significant sample (we typically do 500 human-labeled cases for the final report) to calibrate the automatic thresholds.
[04:10] Jordan: what's the failure mode if automatic and human disagree?
[04:13] Priya: we use human labels as ground truth for final pass/fail. automatic metrics are for fast feedback and gating. if there's disagreement we expand the sample and reconcile. we'll show confidence intervals in the report.
[04:25] Lee: i want to make sure audit trails include which model variant served a request and full traceability for evaluations.
[04:31] Alex: yes, every eval run will have model version, quantization profile, and runtime config recorded. you'll get a per-run artifact bundle with perf traces, token counts, and outputs.
[04:42] Jordan: can you walk through an example golden prompt and how you score it?
[04:47] Priya: sure. e.g. prompt: "Given transaction note 'received payment from Acme Corp invoice 1098', extract payer company and amount in cents." expected: {"payer":"Acme Corp","amount_cents":13500}. automatic scoring: exact-match on JSON fields after normalization. format checks: schema validator rejects free-text or missing fields. hallucination check: ensure payer matches entity in source field; if model invents an extra entity, it's flagged.
[05:20] Samir: what about partial credit? sometimes amount is correct but payer is wrong.
[05:24] Priya: we score per-field; we report per-field precision/recall and an aggregate pass rate. for the POC pass requirement we require all required fields to be correct on at least 92% of golden prompts.
[05:37] Jordan: okay. performance benchmarking — how do you simulate bursty traffic?
[05:41] Alex: we can run synthetic traffic patterns: baseline 1 RPS steady and burst windows up to 50 RPS for 30s to model your spikes. we'll run both hosted shared capacity and dedicated configs so you can see cost vs latency tradeoffs.
[05:55] Marta: our median context length is small — around 120 tokens — but the top 10% go up to 1,200 tokens. how does that affect batching and KV cache?
[06:04] Priya: long contexts change batching efficiency and KV cache pressure. we'll profile with your context-length distribution. for short contexts batching helps cost; for the tail we'll measure memory and p99 latency. side note: auto-transcription might say K V K ache earlier, but we meant KV cache.
[06:22] Lee: on dedicated vs hosted, we need to understand encryption at rest and in transit differences. can dedicated be fully VPC with no egress?
[06:29] Alex: yes, dedicated + private control plane options enable no-egress and customer keys. we'll document network diagrams.
[06:34] Jordan: for the regression playlist, do you support adversarial generation from models to expand edge cases?
[06:39] Priya: yes — we can run adversarial perturbation generators (paraphrase + entity swap) to augment the regression set. those are useful to estimate brittleness.
[06:48] Samir: what's the recommended size for the adversarial augmented set?
[06:51] Priya: typically 1k-3k augmented examples depending on variance. we often do stratified sampling so high-severity intents get more coverage.
[06:58] Jordan: how will you report hallucination types? i.e., fabricated entities vs invented numerical facts.
[07:03] Priya: report will include taxonomy: fabricated-entity, contradictory-fact, hallucinated-attribute. each flagged instance includes generated text, ground truth, auto-detect score, and human label if sampled.
[07:15] Marta: timeline check — you said golden prompts by 3/10 — what about the dedicated test window?
[07:20] Alex: propose 3/16–3/18 for the dedicated benchmark window. report delivered by 3/23 and final review with stakeholders week of 3/24.
[07:31] Jordan: that timeline works provided we get the scripts and evaluation harness to run locally if needed.
[07:36] Priya: we'll open-source the harness for transparency; it'll include the metric exporters and a data canonicalizer.
[07:42] Lee: one more security question — for human eval, will the reviewers see raw user text? we need to ensure PII is masked.
[07:50] Priya: reviewers only see de-identified or syntheticized cases unless you give explicit permission. we can do on-prem human eval if needed.
[07:58] Samir: what are typical pass rates for customers in similar use cases?
[08:02] Priya: it's wide — for domain-specific finance tasks, pre-tuned open models may be 70–85% on golden prompts; with prompt engineering and model selection many get into the 90s. our goal is to demonstrate delta and a path to reach your 92% target within the POC.
[08:19] Jordan: cost side — how should we think about tokens and dedicated pricing?
[08:23] Alex: we'll include an expected token burn estimate in the deck based on sample dataset. dedicated pricing will be expressed as reserved GPU hours + a per-token inference charge for hosted bursts. we'll send a modeled cost spreadsheet.
[08:38] Marta: for benchmarking, what's the required size of the baseline run to be statistically significant?
[08:43] Priya: for primary metrics we recommend at least 2,000 cases for automatic metrics to get ~2–3% margin; for human evaluation we do 500 samples for the final confidence. if you have large logs we can increase sample size.
[08:58] Jordan: any red flags from Redwood's side?
[09:01] Alex: none yet, just standard scoping items — need datasets, access plan, and a decision owner on your side.
[09:08] Samir: decision owner will be Jordan for quality and me for product sign-off.
[09:12] Jordan: agreed.
[09:14] Priya: to recap next technical steps: 1) Marta shares sample dataset and historical failure cases; 2) Alex shares POC runbook, perf checklist, and pricing spreadsheet; 3) Priya shares evaluation harness and baseline scripts; 4) Lee confirms security constraints — all due in the next week.
[09:35] Alex: perfect. i'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark window and a confluence page link.
[09:41] Jordan: thanks everyone. any final questions?
[09:44] Samir: none from product.
[09:46] Lee: nothing else.
[09:47] Marta: all good.
[09:49] Alex: great, we'll close — thanks all.
